messages.subject: bvalue argument interpretation in f()
parts:
Hi all, 

I was working through the example INLA code for the Diggle 2010 paper. What is the bvalue argument in f() used for? I cannot  find any documentation on it. It's used in the following rw2d latent effect. 

### write the formula , model with RW2D latent field ###################
formula = yy ~ alpha + mu0 + mu1 -1 +
  f(ii, model = "rw2d", nrow=nrow, ncol=ncol,
    replicate=replicates ,constr=TRUE, bvalue=1) +
  f(jj, copy = "ii", replicate=replicates,
    fixed=FALSE, param=c(0,0.1))

res = inla(formula, family = c("gaussian", "poisson"), data = data,
           control.family = list(list(initial=1), list()),
           control.inla= list(strategy = "gaussian", int.strategy = "eb"),
           control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE),verbose = TRUE, keep=TRUE)
##############################################################

Thank you!
Thomas

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] bvalue argument interpretation in f()
parts:
you are perfectly correct, that argument is not documented. I'll add
that

bvalue=0 will condition on 0's outside the region, hence the rw2d will
be closer to zero near to the boundary. this model is proper.

bvalue=1 will avoid boundary values all together and create an intrinsic
field (with rank deficiancy=3, unless cyclic). this is the model
described in the GMRF book.

default seems to be bvalue=0.
